nora: heads-up: new int8 canary showing a regression in structured-output parsing on toolcall bench. deploy-bot: canary report: https://infradash/redwood/canaries/17421  spike at ~02:10 UTC :warning:
jiang: what changed?
nora: quant profile changed (per-channel int8) and we tightened batch-window 55ms->30ms for latency tests. prompts unchanged.
priya: sample error:
ERROR: JSONDecodeError: Expecting value at char 0
RESPONSE_SNIPPET: "\\u0000{\"action\":\"notify\",\"args\":{}}"
leading NUL in some outputs.
jiang: likely first-token drift or streaming boundary noise. small/short responses seem overrepresented.
priya: quick mitigations I propose:
- temporary rollback batch-window to 55ms on canary
- deploy lightweight scrub to strip leading control chars <=0x1F before json parse (opt-in for canary)
- enable 1% token-first-token histogram logging for the canary model
- run kv-cache on/off microbench with same prompt set
nora: +1. make scrub cheap and idempotent; keep raw capture for auditing.
deploy-bot: scrub flag deploy started (commit=abc123) est=4m
jiang: also add a gating test to onboarding: run 5k samples and fail if nonprintable-leading-token rate > 0.2%.
priya: opening PR for scrub and telemetry hooks, will include unit test that compares raw vs cleaned outputs.
nora: timeline: rollback now, scrub deploy in ~10m, microbench in parallel. follow-up 10:00am PT.
